applied.problem: Practice states P ÷ S = cos φ and Q = √(S² − P²) absolutely, though explain says this fails for non-sine currents; and P = I²R with the whole current, and the V² ÷ R slip, hold only for series circuits (in parallel R gets the whole voltage). Ships: source says 60 Hz is most common, not universal.

S = 500 VA 'because the current's size does not change as it slides' clashes with the Hold true power screen the same text describes, where it grows; and returned energy goes back towards the supply, not always to it (other loads, or lesson 9's capacitor, take it).
'back to the supply' stops being true after lesson 9 and on screen 12, where the vars slosh between capacitor and coil locally; 'back again' stays true.
The 756 W slip is shown as (5 × 0.87)² × 40, which works out to 757 W; with the unrounded cos φ (1000 ÷ 1150) it is 756 W, the readout.
